slides.heading: Text and Strings
slides.body: Text and Strings is part of Introduction to Python and Output. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Text and Strings
slides.body: A string is text data in Python. Strings are written inside quotation marks, such as "Hello" or "Python".

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A string is like a label on a notebook. The words are meaningful to people, but Python needs the quotation marks to know they are text.

annotations.note: This line stores or updates a value using a variable.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Write one clear instruction at a time. Python reads your code from top to bottom, so order and spelling matter.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Store a short message in a variable named message, then print it.
slides.hint: Put text inside the quotes, then use print(message).

quiz.prompt_text: In Python, what is a string?

options: A whole number without a decimal point
Text data written inside quotation marks
A command that performs a calculation
A symbol used to compare two values

quiz.explanation: Great job! A string is text data in Python, and it must be wrapped in quotation marks so Python knows it is text and not a command.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to store a message in a variable and then display it.
quiz.explanation: First the comment explains the purpose, then the variable is assigned its string value, and finally print() displays the stored message.

quiz.prompt_text: Store a short motivational message in a variable named message, then print it.

content.hint: Put text inside the quotes for message, then use print(message).

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: Assign text to message like message = "Keep going!", then print(message) outputs the stored text. Strings always need quotation marks.
